PullRequest.Title: policy: link "Contact your administrator" to the organization's help page
PullRequest.Body:
Related: https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/30510

Organizations can publish a help page with the new managed setting `communication.support.url`. Wherever VS Code tells users to contact their administrator, it now links to that page, usually through a **Contact Admin** action.

## Problem

When a policy blocks a feature, VS Code says "Contact your administrator." At large organizations most people don't know who administers Copilot, so the message leaves them stuck. Admins had no way to point users to their own help page.

## Repro

1. Disable Agents and set a support URL (Linux paths shown):
   ```jsonc
   // /etc/vscode/policy.json
   { "ChatAgentMode": false }
   // /etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json
   { "communication": { "support": { "url": "https://example.com/copilot-help" } } }
   ```
2. Open the Agents window. **Agents Disabled** offers only a docs link and **Open VS Code**.
3. Repeat the steps: now **Contact Admin** appears. Hovering it shows "Opens your organization's help page (example.com)", and clicking it shows the usual external-website prompt with the full URL.

## What changes

| Surface | Before | After, with a support URL |
|---|---|---|
| Agents window: **Agents Disabled**, **Sign-In Required**, **Managed Settings Unavailable**¹ | "Contact your administrator" with no link | **Contact Admin** button |
| Account restriction notification | **Sign In** · **Learn More** | **Sign In** · **Contact Admin** · **Learn More** |
| **Remote Connections** policy footer | "…Contact your administrator. **View Setting**" | "…disabled by your organization. **Contact Admin**" |
| **Customizations > MCP Servers** and **Plugins** when disabled by policy | Plain text | "Contact your administrator for more information." is a link |
| Model picker, on a model a Business or Enterprise admin hasn't enabled | **Contact your admin** opens GitHub's Copilot settings | **Contact Admin** opens the organization's help page |

¹ Except when the fix is to sign in, wait out a rate limit or update VS Code.

- Without the setting, or with an invalid value, nothing new appears and there is no default help page. The model picker still links to GitHub's Copilot settings, and Remote Connections still offers **View Setting**.
- Only absolute `http` or `https` URLs are used, so `javascript:` and `file:` values are ignored. The page always opens in the external browser through link protection, including on middle-click, so untrusted domains still prompt first. Keyboard users can operate that prompt while the Agents overlay is up.
- An open account restriction notification updates if the URL changes; one the user closed stays closed. An open model picker or Remote Connections menu closes instead, so reopening it shows the current link.
- Every blocking Agents overlay now scrolls when its card doesn't fit, and Tab moves into the card and wraps within it, with or without a support URL. When the URL changes, the overlay keeps focus on the same action.
- **Policy Diagnostics** shows which channel supplied the communication block, and lists a support URL excluded by a higher-priority block.
- `communication` follows the runtime's whole-block channel precedence, like `telemetry`. It is informational only: an organization that sets just this block is not treated as managing Copilot settings.

## Before / After

## Notes

- Sign-In Required, Managed Settings Unavailable and the locked model need a restricted account, a failed refresh or a Business plan, so their screenshots come from the new `…WithSupport` component fixtures.
- Not covered yet: permission picker hovers, quota and sandbox messages, MCP allowlist messages, and the Copilot extension's own messages.

Scenarios.Scenario: Managed settings are loaded at startup or changed from file/native/server delivery, then effective policy and support URL consumers update.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing channel delivery completes first; normalization and pickManagedSettings synchronously flatten and merge the bounded settings bag, equality-check the effective bag, and only then notify in-memory consumers. The PR adds one whole-block lookup over a fixed two-element array per key and local URL parsing in listeners; no new I/O is placed on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse managed-settings.json after a watched file change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per coalesced file-change burst, with a 1 MB size limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same watched, throttled file read and parse occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read must finish before file-delivered settings can update, but all PR-added support consumers run after it and do not cause another read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of normalized managed-setting leaves across three channels; file input is already capped at 1 MB, and whole-block classification examines exactly two block names per key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File changes are coalesced by the existing 500 ms ThrottledDelayer; effective-setting changes are emitted synchronously once after equality comparison, and UI listeners execute serially on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The account policy service retains the previous effective bag and suppresses unchanged events. Sessions overlays compare full options, customization widgets retain a message key, and open picker/menu listeners compare the currently shown support URL before changing UI.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the merge loops, equality gate, throttler, and added listeners were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Enterprise settings key counts vary, but the added classification factor is fixed at two blocks and notifications occur only when the effective bag changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new boundary call or unbounded work was added, and repeated UI work is gated by equality or presentation keys.

Scenarios.Scenario: A policy-blocked Agents surface renders, receives layout/focus events, and optionally opens the organization help page.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Overlay construction now creates one DomScrollableElement and scans one small card; subsequent main-container layouts synchronously read its client/scroll dimensions and reveal the focused action. This affects only the active full-window blocking overlay. Opening support is off the render/layout path and requires a click.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the configured organization support URL in the external browser through the opener service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one opener invocation per explicit Contact Admin click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No organization support navigation existed from these overlay actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not on overlay render, focus, resize, or policy-update critical paths; only the click awaits/starts external navigation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One overlay, one card, and a small fixed number of actions; layout work scales with window-layout events while the blocking overlay is present, not with repository or session size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM/layout work is serialized on the UI thread; focus reveal is coalesced to the next animation frame for focus-in events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The contribution retains current overlay options and skips reconstruction when they are equal; URL changes intentionally replace the single overlay while preserving focus.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new scanDomNode calls synchronously read four dimensions, but they are scoped to one visible blocking card.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resize frequency and browser layout cost vary, but the DOM cardinality is fixed and tiny.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the generalized scroll work is bounded to one small overlay and is necessary to keep actions reachable; it does not scale with product data or add boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: MCP Servers or Plugins customization UI is disabled by policy and managed settings change while the widget exists.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The managed-settings event calls updateAccessState, which performs local configuration inspection and DOM class updates. Disabled-message reconstruction and hover/listener replacement occur only when the policy-lock/support-URL message key changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the organization support page externally after link activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener invocation per click or middle-click; there is no per-server or per-plugin call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The policy-disabled message was plain text and initiated no support navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the managed-settings and widget-render critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two widget instances at most for the touched surfaces, each with one disabled message and one link; work does not scale with installed servers or plugins on unchanged support settings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Listeners run serially; existing gallery/connector work is cancelled when access is disabled, with no new asynchronous work started by support URL handling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: renderedDisabledMessage is a positive presentation cache keyed by lock state and support URL; unchanged updates preserve the DOM node, focus, hover, and listener. Disposal remains owned by each widget and MutableDisposable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both updateAccessState implementations and their cleanup ownership were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Widget lifetime varies, but retained state is one string and one disposable per widget.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: message caching prevents repeated DOM allocation, listener ownership is bounded, and navigation is user-triggered rather than collection-fanned out.

Scenarios.Scenario: The model picker opens with admin-locked models, reacts to a managed support URL change, and optionally follows Contact Admin.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Picker open reads and validates the in-memory support URL once, creates one support descriptor, and passes it into existing unavailable-row construction. Each locked row constructs its existing description with the selected URL. A settings event only parses the URL and hides the picker if that URL changed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the organization support page externally when a locked-model Contact Admin link is clicked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener invocation for the selected link click, independent of model count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The row opened the existing GitHub settings URL or showed plain text; the organization URL adds no extra call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off picker-open and row-render critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of unavailable featured models shown in the picker after existing filtering; one shared URL/tooltip descriptor is resolved per picker open, with bounded string escaping per unavailable row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Picker construction and event handling are synchronous and serialized; no remote reads are launched by the PR.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The URL is snapshotted for the open picker in _shownSupportUrl; unrelated managed-setting changes retain the picker, while an actual URL change closes it to avoid rebuilding stale links.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: picker open, row creation, settings listener, and click handler were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of unavailable models varies, but the added per-row work is short string escaping and does not cross a boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no eager network work or per-model boundary fan-out was introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remote Connections policy menu or account-restriction notification displays Contact Admin and responds to support URL changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu/notification creation reads the in-memory support URL and creates one action. Managed-setting events compare against the shown URL; only an actual URL change hides the menu or closes and recreates the one open notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the configured organization support page externally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener call per explicit action click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Remote Connections opened local settings and the notification had no organization support action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required to display or refresh either UI surface.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One menu or one sticky notification per surface, independent of repositories, models, or remote connection count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates are synchronous and serialized; external opening occurs only from action.run.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The menu stores its shown policy-footer URL, and the notification stores its key and shown URL. Unrelated setting changes are no-ops; notification dismissal state remains separately persisted.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the stored URL guards and notification/menu lifecycle were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Managed-setting changes are deployment-dependent, but unchanged effective values are suppressed upstream and unchanged support URLs are ignored locally.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: refresh work is coalesced by value comparison, retained state is constant-sized, and external work is click-driven.

Scenarios.Scenario: Policy Diagnostics is explicitly invoked and renders managed-settings provenance including communication block selection.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command already gathers and projects all managed settings. The PR adds fixed-count filtering/source scans and one extra summary row while constructing the in-memory Markdown report.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of effective and excluded setting keys; the added block-source scan is performed twice for exactly two known whole blocks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous command execution; no parallel or repeated scheduling is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used because diagnostics is an explicit snapshot command; source data is already resident in services.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full changed diagnostic construction block was inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Diagnostic bag size varies up to existing managed-settings bounds, but the added passes are linear with a constant count and only run on explicit invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the small additional linear scans are off normal startup/render paths and add no serialization or I/O boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review across all 26 changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup/change propagation, blocked-overlay layout, customization widgets, model picker, Remote Connections, notifications, diagnostics, support-link lifecycle, and external opener boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
